caption: The drawing is a technical illustration of a block front mahogany desk from the period 1780-1775, attributed to Lawrence Phillips. The drawing is composed in black ink on a beige or off-white background, and contains four main views: a plan of the top, a front elevation, a side elevation, and a detailed view of the desk with its lid open. The plan of the top is a rectangular outline showing the desk’s surface with dimensions of 32 inches by 17 1/2 inches, and a second width notation of 30 inches. The front elevation depicts the desk's height of 36 inches and a block-front design, with a drawer section below, containing three large drawers and two smaller side drawers above, each with ornate handles, and a scalloped apron with cabriole legs ending in ball-and-claw feet. The side elevation shows the profile of the desk, including a projecting section at the front and a sloped lid, with additional dimensions noted as 12 inches and 9 inches for the respective sections. The detailed view with the lid open reveals a fitted interior with multiple small drawers, vertical pigeonholes, and a central arched compartment, flanked by columns. Text on the right side identifies the desk's type, wood, date, and the creator of the drawing. The scale is indicated as 1/8 inch equals 1 foot.
title: Child's Desk
